question: What dissipative material measurement converts a conventional graphite mode calculation to a low-frequency drag coefficient, and how does its load slope enter?
assumptions: The archived fixed-roster KC-plus-1.44-eV-plate stationary 14-height model supplies a conventional C and positive K, with one 12C upper-site mass and rigid lower sheet.
A weakly damped open material bath has a Rayleigh D diagonal in the conservative eigenbasis and a shared width inside each E pair.
Resolved spectral FWHM represents dissipative pole broadening after finite-time and instrument deconvolution.
The moving-contact force estimator is not inferred from low-frequency gamma alone.
physical_mapping: CONDITIONAL conventional Cartesian lateral and height coordinates; physical linewidths, off-diagonal loss and UD additive coupling OPEN
target_exposure: The paired angles and near-zero load response were known; the archived conventional mode and pressure sweeps predate this calculation; no experimental linewidth or friction fit.
fitted_choices: No new fitted parameters; inherited plate D=1.44 eV, 12C mass, fixed-roster cutoff and C3 registry are prior illustrative material choices
baseline: Closed harmonic height model has zero Ohmic drag; conventional open phonon/contact bath with measured retarded linewidths
result: CONDITIONAL/NUMERICAL at archived 16 A reference: gamma_scalar=(2.7634530847e-4 Delta_f_L+1.8676114422e-5 Delta_f_H) meV ps/A^2 per atom for widths in THz, assuming diagonal mode damping and high Q. Low pair contributes 93.6696% for equal widths. Equal constant widths give logarithmic drag slope +8.06052e-4 per MPa; linewidth pressure derivatives remain unknown.
